items.followUp: What is a coordinate covalent bond? Give one example.

rubric.why: A covalent bond is defined by the sharing of electrons between atoms.
rubric.description: Defines a covalent bond as sharing of electron pair(s) between atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atoms mutually share one or more electron pairs.

rubric.why: A correct example demonstrates the definition.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of a covalent molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any valid covalent molecule, such as H₂, CH₄ or Cl₂.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is formed when atoms mutually share one or more pairs of electrons.
For example, the two hydrogen atoms in H₂ share an electron pair.

items.followUp: Why does the density of a gas decrease when it is heated at constant pressure?

rubric.why: Cooling causes a gas to contract when the pressure is constant.
rubric.description: States that the gas volume decreases on cooling.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that cooling makes the gas contract or its volume decrease.

rubric.why: Density is mass per unit volume, so a smaller volume for the same mass means greater density.
rubric.description: Connects the decreased volume to increased density for the same mass of gas.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that density increases because the same mass occupies less volume.

modelAnswer: On cooling at constant pressure, a gas contracts and its volume decreases.
For the same mass of gas, the smaller volume gives a greater density (density = mass ÷ volume).

items.followUp: Define a concentrated solution and state what concentration measures.

rubric.why: A dilute solution has relatively little solute compared with its solvent.
rubric.description: Defines a dilute solution in terms of a small amount of solute relative to solvent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a dilute solution contains a small amount of solute in a relatively large amount of solvent.

rubric.why: Concentration expresses how much solute is present in a specified amount of solution.
rubric.description: Defines concentration as the amount of solute in a given amount of solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating the amount of solute to a specified amount or volume of solution.

modelAnswer: A dilute solution contains a small amount of solute dissolved in a relatively large amount of solvent.
Concentration is the amount of solute dissolved in a given amount of solution.

items.followUp: Why does iodine dissolve in hexane but not readily in water?

rubric.why: Naphthalene is a non-polar substance, as is carbon tetrachloride.
rubric.description: Identifies naphthalene and carbon tetrachloride as non-polar substances.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying naphthalene as non-polar and linking it to non-polar carbon tetrachloride.

rubric.why: Polar water does not dissolve non-polar naphthalene well; substances with similar polarity tend to dissolve one another.
rubric.description: Explains its poor solubility in water using polarity or the principle “like dissolves like.”
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that water is polar and naphthalene is non-polar, or correctly applying “like dissolves like.”

modelAnswer: Naphthalene and carbon tetrachloride are non-polar, so naphthalene dissolves in carbon tetrachloride.
Water is polar, so it does not dissolve non-polar naphthalene well; like dissolves like.

items.followUp: Why is milk classified as a colloid?

rubric.why: A colloid consists of particles of one substance dispersed in another.
rubric.description: Identifies blood particles or proteins as dispersed in plasma.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a dispersed phase in plasma.

rubric.why: Colloidal particles remain dispersed and have characteristic colloidal behaviour.
rubric.description: States a characteristic that supports classifying blood as a colloid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for noting that the dispersed particles remain suspended, are colloidal in size, or scatter light.

modelAnswer: Blood contains particles, including cells and proteins, dispersed in plasma.
These particles remain suspended in the plasma, so blood shows the behaviour of a colloid.

items.followUp: Define reduction in terms of electrons and give an example.

rubric.why: Oxidation is defined in terms of electron loss.
rubric.description: Defines oxidation as the loss of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that oxidation is loss of electrons.

rubric.why: A suitable equation must show a species losing electrons.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of oxidation by electron loss.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct oxidation half-equation, such as Na → Na⁺ + e⁻.

modelAnswer: Oxidation is the loss of one or more electrons.

items.followUp: Why does the reactivity of alkali metals increase down Group 1?

rubric.why: Atoms become larger down a group, placing the outermost electron farther from the nucleus.
rubric.description: States that atomic size increases and the outer electron is farther from the nucleus down the group.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the increase in atomic radius or increased distance of the outer electron.

rubric.why: The outer electron is lost more easily, so the metal reacts more readily.
rubric.description: Connects the increased size to easier electron loss and greater reactivity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that electron loss becomes easier or ionization energy decreases, increasing reactivity.

modelAnswer: Down a group, the atomic size increases and the outermost electron is farther from the nucleus.
This electron is lost more easily, so the reactivity of metals increases down the group.

items.followUp: Why is copper used for making cooking utensils?

rubric.why: Electrical wires need a material that conducts electricity well.
rubric.description: States that copper is a good conductor of electricity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying copper’s high electrical conductivity.

rubric.why: A wire material must be capable of being drawn into thin strands.
rubric.description: States that copper is ductile and can be drawn into wires.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying copper’s ductility or its ability to be drawn into wires.

modelAnswer: Copper is a good conductor of electricity.
It is ductile, so it can be drawn into thin wires.
